title: Reuse bridge JVM processes across golden tests to avoid slow per-test JVM startup
description:
Each golden test currently spawns fresh JVM processes for the replay client (and potato client). Starting a JVM, loading classes, and initializing the MCP bridge takes several seconds per process. With 8+ golden tests, this adds up significantly.

Investigate keeping the bridge JVM processes alive across tests within the same pytest session, similar to how the XMage server is already reused via the session-scoped xmage_server fixture. The bridge client would need to support reconnecting to a new game table without restarting the JVM. This could be done via an MCP tool (e.g. `reset` or `join_table`) or by making the bridge's game-joining logic reentrant.

Key considerations:
- The replay client (puppeteer/src/puppeteer/replay.py) spawns a new bridge process per test via StdioServerParameters
- The potato client is also a fresh JVM per test
- State isolation between tests must be preserved (ShortIdRegistry, game state, etc.)
- The MCP session lifecycle is tied to the JVM process; reuse would require either keeping the stdio pipe open or switching to a persistent transport
